tools.name: check_agent
tools.description: Checks a finished agent file against the template rules (manifest, naming, class, perform method, no hardcoded secrets). Call it on every agent you write, fix anything it reports, and call it again until it passes.

tools.description: Searches the public agent registry (about 1,700 single-file agents) for agents that already do what the user wants, for example when they ask 'is there an AI tool for...' or want a ready-made automation instead of building one. tools.description: Returns the full source of one agent from the registry, by its name (e.g. @bill/neuron_agent), so it can be read or adapted.

tools.name: use_agent_here

tools.name: how_to_run_agent
tools.description: Optional, for later: how to keep an agent running on the user's own computer with the free Brainstem. Only offer this after the user has used the agent in the chat and wants to keep it.

tools.name: share_agent
tools.description: Use only when the user says they want to share an agent they built. Checks the agent and scans it for personal details (emails, phone numbers, secrets), then explains how to publish it to the free public agent registry under their own GitHub account. Nothing is published by this tool.

tools.name: request_service
tools.description: Use when the person wants something none of these tools can do and says yes to passing the request on. Records only the request text they agree to send (no name or contact). Ask before calling it.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_agent_template, use_agent_here · Private data: get_agent_template, check_agent, find_agents, share_agent, request_service · Public sink: share_agent, request_service · Destructive: use_agent_here, how_to_run_agent.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_agent_template, use_agent_here · Private data: get_agent_template, check_agent, find_agents, share_agent, request_service · Public sink: share_agent, request_service · Destructive: use_agent_here, how_to_run_agent

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
